answer: The anchor of the orchard in an agent economy resists sybil attacks by maintaining a shared ledger of transaction histories for every identity. A whisper protocol monitors for anomalous signals that indicate potential clones. When signals are detected, the system flags the duplicate identities and burns a portion of their bonds as penalty. Consequently, an attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities must expend 42,000 POA per identity in total, with the cost increasing linearly as the number of duplicates grows, while genuine operators pay nothing.
